faq.title: Frequently asked questions

q1.q: Do I need a residence permit to live in Istanbul?
q1.a: Yes. To stay legally beyond your visa or visa-free period you need a residence permit (İkamet). The most common first permit is the short-term one, usually valid for 1–2 years. Start by getting a tax number and mandatory health insurance, then apply on the e-İkamet portal.

q2.q: How do I open a bank account as a foreigner?
q2.a: You generally need your passport, a Turkish tax number (Vergi No), and proof of address. Requirements vary by bank and even by branch — if one refuses, another may accept you. Your card usually arrives by courier within a week.

q3.q: What is a Vergi No and how do I get one?
q3.a: It is your Turkish tax number, required for banking, rentals and most official steps. It is free and takes minutes online via the İnteraktif Vergi Dairesi portal, or about an hour at any tax office.

q4.q: Is it true some Istanbul districts are closed to new residents?
q4.a: Yes. A number of Istanbul districts are closed to new residence-permit registrations at any given time. Always verify your specific district is open BEFORE signing a rental contract, or your application can be rejected.

q5.q: Can I get Turkish citizenship by buying property?
q5.a: Property investment can make you eligible to apply for citizenship — it does not guarantee approval. You must buy above the official threshold and hold the property for three years; the final decision belongs solely to the Turkish government after its own review. Listings marked “Meets citizenship threshold” satisfy the investment amount, and our legal team verifies every title deed, but no purchase can promise citizenship itself.

q6.q: How does the free expert appointment work?
q6.a: When the AI assistant sees that your case needs a human, it offers a free online appointment (call or video). You only pick a date, time and language — your problem summary and chat are attached automatically for the specialist.

istanbulkart.title: Istanbulkart: the only transport card you need
istanbulkart.excerpt: Metro, bus, tram, ferry — one card for everything.
istanbulkart.body: Buy an Istanbulkart at any metro station kiosk or machine for a small card fee, then top it up with cash or card. It works on metro, Metrobüs, buses, trams, funiculars and city ferries, and transfers within two hours are discounted. One card can pay for multiple passengers. Keep it topped up — drivers don't sell tickets.

esim.title: eSIM vs airport SIM: don't overpay
esim.excerpt: Airport SIM kiosks charge tourists double. Here's the smart way.
esim.body: SIM packages sold at the airport are heavily marked up. If your phone supports eSIM, buy a Turkish eSIM online before flying and land connected. For a physical SIM, any Turkcell, Vodafone or Türk Telekom shop in the city is far cheaper than the airport. Note: foreign phones must be registered (a paid IMEI registration) if you stay beyond 90 days with a Turkish SIM.

ikamet.title: İkamet: residence permit from A to Z
ikamet.excerpt: The full application flow, documents, and the closed-district trap.
ikamet.body: The residence permit (ikamet) flow: get a tax number, buy mandatory health insurance, register your address with a notarized rental contract, then apply on the e-İkamet portal and attend your appointment with biometric photos and document copies. Critical: a number of Istanbul districts are closed to new registrations at any given time — verify your district is open BEFORE you sign a rental contract.

vergi.title: Vergi No: your Turkish tax number
vergi.excerpt: Free, fast, and required for almost everything.
vergi.body: The tax number (Vergi Numarası) is required to open a bank account, sign contracts, buy property and apply for residence. Get it free online via the İnteraktif Vergi Dairesi portal with your passport details, or in person at any tax office (Vergi Dairesi) in about an hour. Keep the printout — banks ask for it.

bank.title: Opening a Turkish bank account
bank.excerpt: Which banks accept foreigners and what they ask for.
bank.body: Requirements vary by bank and even by branch. You will always need your passport and tax number; most banks also want proof of address (notarized rental contract or a utility bill in your name) and sometimes a residence permit. If one branch refuses, try another — policies genuinely differ. Your card typically arrives by courier within a week.

districts.title: Choosing your district in Istanbul
districts.excerpt: Character, prices and the residence-permit factor.
districts.body: Kadıköy and Beşiktaş offer central, lively living at higher rents; Üsküdar is calmer and conservative; Esenyurt and Beylikdüzü are budget-friendly but far; Şişli and Levent suit professionals. Before falling in love with a flat, check two things: whether the district is open for new residence-permit registrations, and your commute on the metro map.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.body:
Welcome to Rafiq Istanbul. By creating an account or using our website and services, you agree to these Terms.

1. Who we are. Rafiq Istanbul is an independent guidance and concierge service that helps foreigners settle in Istanbul. We are not a government agency, a law firm, or an official authority, and we do not issue any official document. Government fees and timelines are set by the relevant authorities, not by us.

2. Your account. You are responsible for the accuracy of the information you provide and for keeping your login credentials secure. You must be at least 18 years old to purchase a subscription.

3. Subscriptions and billing. Paid plans are billed in advance for the chosen period (monthly or annual) and renew automatically until you cancel. You can cancel at any time from the Pricing page; your access continues until the end of the period already paid.

4. Our services. Some services are delivered directly by our team; others are arranged through vetted partner offices. Estimates of fees and durations are indicative and confirmed before work begins. We act as a guide and facilitator and cannot guarantee the outcome of any official application, which depends on the relevant authority.

5. Acceptable use. You agree not to misuse the platform, submit false information, or use our services for unlawful purposes.

6. Liability. To the maximum extent permitted by law, Rafiq Istanbul is not liable for indirect or consequential damages, or for decisions made by third parties or official authorities.

7. Changes. We may update these Terms or our services from time to time. Continued use after changes means you accept the updated Terms.

8. Governing law. These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Türkiye.

9. Contact. For any question about these Terms, contact our team through the app.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy (KVKK)
privacy.body:
This Privacy Policy explains how Rafiq Istanbul collects and uses your information, in line with the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law (KVKK No. 6698).

1. Data we collect. Account details (name, email), the answers you give during onboarding, your service requests and bookings, documents you choose to upload, and basic usage data needed to operate the service.

2. Why we use it. To provide and personalize our services, prepare and follow up your requests, communicate with you, and improve the platform. We do not sell your personal data.

3. Sharing. We share only what is necessary with the vetted partner handling your specific request (for example, a translation office or insurance provider). Our infrastructure is hosted on secure cloud providers.

4. Storage and security. Your data is stored on protected servers with access controls. Uploaded documents stay private to your account and are accessible to our team only to deliver the service you requested.

5. Your rights (KVKK). You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data, and you may withdraw consent at any time, by contacting us.

6. Retention. We keep your data only as long as needed to provide the service and meet legal obligations, then delete or anonymize it.

7. Contact. For privacy requests, contact our team through the app.

refund.title: Refund and Return Policy
refund.body:
Last updated: 2026-07-21

1. Scope
This policy applies to all paid services offered through the Rafiq Istanbul platform, including residence permits, tax number, banking, housing, health, and education services.

2. Government Fees
All fees paid directly to government authorities or official institutions (e.g., Immigration Office, Tax Department) are non-refundable once the application has been submitted to the relevant authority.

3. Rafiq Istanbul Service Fees
Mediation and service fees are refundable according to the following schedule:
- Service not yet started: Full refund (100%) within 14 business days of request.
- Document collection phase: Partial refund (50%) within 14 business days.
- Application submitted to authorities: No refund on service fees.

4. Subscriptions
Monthly subscriptions can be cancelled at any time. Access continues until the end of the current billing period with no partial refund.

5. Refund Request
Refund requests should be sent to: support@rafiq-istanbul.com with the order number and service details. Processing takes up to 14 business days.

6. Non-eligible Refunds
No refund shall be issued in the following cases: submission of false information, or applications rejected due to invalid documents provided by the client.

7. Governing Law
This policy is governed by the applicable laws of the Republic of Türkiye, Istanbul.

edevlet.title: e-Devlet — the master key
edevlet.body: Turkey's official government app. With your foreigner ID (Yabancı Kimlik No) you can view your residence permit, book appointments, download official documents, check your address registration and more — all in one place.

eikamet.title: e-İkamet (Göç İdaresi)

istanbulkart.title: Istanbulkart app
istanbulkart.body: Top up your transport card straight from your phone — no kiosk needed. It also shows your balance and the nearest ferry, metro and bus lines.

bitaksi.title: BiTaksi / iTaksi
bitaksi.body: Hail a licensed, metered taxi from the app so you always pay the real fare. The trip and driver are logged — far safer than flagging one on the street.

getir.title: Getir & Yemeksepeti
getir.body: Groceries in minutes and food delivery from almost anywhere. Pay by card in-app — handy before your Turkish bank account is ready.

esim.title: Buy an eSIM before you land
esim.body: An eSIM bought online is far cheaper than SIM cards sold at the airport, and you arrive already connected to book taxis and find your way.

vergi.title: Get your Vergi No online first
vergi.body: Your tax number is free from the İnteraktif Vergi Dairesi portal in minutes. Get it before the bank visit — most branches ask for it.

taxiCaution.title: Never ride an unmetered taxi
taxiCaution.body: Insist on the meter ("taksimetre") or use a taxi app. Agreeing a price by hand on day one is the most common way newcomers overpay.
